title: AI Bots Alert! Shopping AI Agents Are Redefining Agentic Traffic
summary: Meta’s Muse becomes the top declared AI bot ahead of Black Friday. Will ChatGPT Wallet be next?
body_markdown:
**By Gilit Saporta, VP Fraud and Quality, and Yuval Rubin, Director, Product Management, Conversational AI Ads**


Black Friday is here, and shopping AI agents are everywhere. Automated web traffic in 2026 has crossed every threshold, with scrapers and AI-powered bots operating in higher volume than ever before. Q4 of 2026 is expected to close with unprecedented levels of automated browsing activity and brands are eager to know which portion of this surge will impact their spend.


As seen above, November is already showing a surge in automated browsing, tripling in volume in just one month. However, the overall surge of AI-powered activity is not new. Last year, DV’s Fraud Lab reported an


[86% increase in GIVT](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/verify/ai-crawlers-and-scrapers-are-contributing-to-an-increase-in-general-invalid-traffic) , largely attributed to AI crawlers and scrapers. Back then, Meta’s AI crawler reached second place in impact, among all declared AI bots.


## What Do AI Bots Mean to Adtech?


Adtech has long relied on being able to measure consumers’ exposure to ads, as well as their attention and intent (estimated based on searching, browsing and clicking). Personal AI agents are shifting this paradigm by acting as intermediaries between the consumer and the web. These agentic assistants don't just retrieve information; they execute multi-step tasks, curate options and facilitate purchases on the user's behalf. As this technology moves from concept to commercial reality, consumer adoption is accelerating.


Two recent product launches highlight this rapid mainstream integration. Instinct by Spear Street and Muse by Meta have quickly emerged as leading players in the agentic space. Following its August release, Instinct reported reaching[100,000 users](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/ai-agent-startup-instinct-talks-10-billion-valuation) in just two weeks. Muse, released shortly after in early September, illustrates an even larger scale with 10 million users in 40 days,


[25% of whom](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/shopping-muse-top-task-meta-111133132.html) were already shopping through Muse, with an average purchase size of $200.


DV’s data shows that in 2026, Meta’s Muse quickly became the fastest-growing AI bot, and its impact was felt industry-wide, including adtech. When Meta rolled out Muse, a personal agent capable of executing multi-step tasks inside an isolated cloud-hosted browser environment, it bypassed the gradual adoption curve typical of new web crawlers. Backed by Meta’s massive consumer distribution, Muse immediately began traversing the open web to browse, compare and transact on behalf of millions of users.


The immediate telemetry impact of Muse’s initial rollout was unprecedented. Within its very first days of detected live traffic, Muse spiked to over one million daily impressions on monitored inventory according to DV internal data. Its massive impact generated over nine times the impressions volume of the average declared AI agent.


Why do shopping agents like Muse produce impressions? The answer lies in the way that Muse accessed its target websites. Muse often opted for web scraping when attempting to complete a purchase or a task. DV Fraud Lab


[research](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/verify/swat-that-bot-new-dv-tools-keep-the-wrong-kind-of-ai-away-from-your-ad-spend) shows what that looks like in the data. In a simulated shopping exercise, a researcher asked Perplexity's Comet browser to find and buy body lotion. On the way to checkout, Comet reported dozens of “clicking” and "searching" interactions, with no human needed at the screen.


What were the AI agents doing? They were clicking, often excessively and repeatedly. In DV's testing, AI bots that produced impressions accounted for up to 15% of all clicks in unprotected media. In certain client-testing and research studies, an ad click was 10 times more likely to be from an AI bot than from a human.


For many ad operations and security engineering teams, it became important to distinguish these user-directed sessions from the overall volume of invalid traffic (IVT). This required deep behavioral and infrastructure telemetry, which was available thanks to


[DV AI Verification™](https://doubleverify.com/company/newsroom/doubleverify-introduces-dv-ai-verification-offering-to-identify-and-manage-agent-interactions-and-avoid-ai-slop) (which adds transparency for brands who seek a granular view of AI bots impacting their traffic), launched in 2025.


In mid-November, Muse shifted gears again. Operating at scale without declared identity created potential friction in the digital supply chain. To solve this risk for operational breakdown, Meta adopted protocols to allow its activity to become self-declared.


As soon as Muse transitioned into a cryptographically verifiable protocol, DV was ready to support the new change and incorporate it into the existing declared AI Bot reporting within DV’s AI verification suite. DV was already tracking and reporting AI bots that use emerging protocols for AI agent authentication protocols (such as Web Bot Auth). Traffic associated with these protocols will typically be disclosed as general invalid traffic (GIVT). Importantly, DV is an active member of the MRC’s AI Working Group to shape how such traffic might be considered in the future, given the fast evolution of AI-powered traffic and its potential implications for brands.


## Where Would Agentic Traffic Go Next?


The AI race seems to be never-ending. In mid November, OpenAI launched the ChatGPT Wallet. Now, ChatGPT’s "Dots" AI agents are able to complete online purchases on users' behalf through merchants' existing checkouts.


Should OpenAI expand Wallet access beyond its current region and tiers, it could challenge Muse for dominance in high-intent retail and checkout environments. DV will be there, as always, to verify what's real and make sense of what's new.


The value of independent measurement in the emerging environment of conversational AI ads cannot be overlooked. This is why DV has already introduced its


[AI Verification](https://doubleverify.com/company/newsroom/doubleverify-introduces-dv-ai-verification-offering-to-identify-and-manage-agent-interactions-and-avoid-ai-slop) solutions in 2025. Furthermore, DV


[announced its launch](https://doubleverify.com/company/newsroom/dv-launches-attribution-measurement-and-advances-brand-suitability-for-chatgpt-ads) for attribution measurement and advanced brand suitability for ChatGPT Ads in October 2026.
